Go To Content ::: Home > Water Basics > Definitions > Total dissolved solids (TDS) Definitions Total dissolved solids (TDS) Release Time： 22020-05-28 Tags： Definitions Total dissolved solids (TDS) is the total amount of solids dissolved in the water, including soluble hydrogen carbonate ions, chloride salts, sulphates, calcium, magnesium, sodium, potassium, volatile solids and non-volatile solids. Its concentration will affect the taste of drinking water. A way to measure it is to filter the water sample (0.45μm), dry the solution at the temperature of 103℃ to 105℃ and then weigh the remaining residuals.
